clue.text: Summon back to city demonstrating ludicrous change

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England
to cite someone is to summon them to appear in court

explanation.surface: Someone is recalled to the city, and the move is somehow absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: To cite is to summon formally, as a court does a witness; Bath is a Somerset city. 'Ludicrous change' points to bathos, a comic drop from the lofty to the trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathos is a ludicrous descent from the elevated to the trivial, and the adjective describes writing that makes that comic drop.

clue.text: Physicist — one going on and on endlessly about hydrogen

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is dropped from the word
about means surrounding, so one piece is placed around another

blocks.note: a bore is a person who drones on tediously
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A physicist is described as a tedious talker who never stops about hydrogen.
explanation.walkthrough: BORE loses its last letter to become BOR, which then wraps around H.
explanation.definitionFit: Niels Bohr was the Danish scientist who modelled the atom, starting with the hydrogen atom, so he is a famous example.

clue.text: Rubbish seen round top of railway cutting

indicators.note: the top of a down entry word is its first letter, so only that letter is kept
to go round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: tat is cheap, worthless junk
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Litter is spotted around the start of a railway cutting, the trench a line runs through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Railway cutting' reads as one thing, but 'cutting' is split off as the definition, meaning sharp or sarcastic.
explanation.definitionFit: A tart remark and a cutting remark are both sharp, biting and hurtful, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Intelligence calculates pi on a general sequence

indicators.note: a sequence is an unbroken run of letters, here read straight across the word breaks

blocks.note: the run starts at the end of the first word and stops inside the last

explanation.surface: A clever machine works out the digits of pi in some ordered sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from calculatES through PI ON A to GEneral, giving ESPIONAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligence in the military sense is gathering secret information, which is exactly what spying achieves.

clue.text: Dark beer, pint, drunk with meal

indicators.note: someone drunk is jumbled and unsteady, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pint of dark beer, such as stout, is downed alongside a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark' looks like an adjective for the beer, but it is the definition, meaning obscure or impossible to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dark in the sense of mysterious or obscure cannot be penetrated by the mind or by light.

clue.text: Mineral of thulium also containing aluminium and copper

indicators.note: to contain is to hold inside, so the outer piece wraps the others

blocks.note: Tm is the chemical symbol for thulium
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, from Latin cuprum

explanation.surface: A chemist describes a mineral made of thulium with traces of aluminium and copper.
explanation.walkthrough: All three elements are given by their chemical symbols, with TM split open to hold the other two.
explanation.definitionFit: Talcum is the soft mineral talc, best known ground into the powder used after bathing.

clue.text: Dread admitting a king’s return to the land of the living

definitions.text: return to the land of the living

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the outer piece takes the others inside

blocks.note: awe is reverential fear or dread
taken as written
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Dread grips a nation as its king comes back from the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' looks like a reversal signal, but it belongs to the definition, a verb meaning to come round.
explanation.definitionFit: To awake is to rouse from sleep, figuratively coming back to life and consciousness after a deathlike rest.

clue.text: Possibly a green method of recycling maps

blocks.note: to map an area is to chart it
using something again is one way of recycling it

explanation.surface: An eco-friendly way of recycling old maps is suggested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks environmental, matching recycling, but it is a colour; 'of' puts the recycling after the maps.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartreuse is a yellowish-green shade named after the liqueur, so it is one example of a green, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: I left in changed form, such as Mr Hyde was known to do

definitions.text: such as Mr Hyde was known to do

indicators.note: placed in something means put inside it, so the short pieces sit within the longer one

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the standard abbreviation for left
a mutation is an altered form

explanation.surface: A changed form, like Jekyll turning into Hyde, is what the clue seems to describe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changed form' tempts as an anagram signal; it is the word MUTATION, which takes I and L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Hyde in Stevenson's novel brutally attacks people, and violent maiming of bodies is the kind of thing he did.

clue.text: Dance one spied regularly around Royal Navy?

definitions.text: Dance one spied regularly around Royal Navy?

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
to go around something is to enclose it

blocks.note: a hop is an informal dance
the Roman numeral for one
the second and fourth letters of the word
RN is the standard abbreviation for the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A dance is glimpsed now and then around the navy, a sailors' jig.
explanation.walkthrough: HOP, I and PE together surround RN; the whole clue then describes the result, since this dance is famously performed by sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: The hornpipe is a lively solo dance traditionally associated with sailors of the British navy.

clue.text: Rock at the lowest level beginning on top

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is kept

blocks.note: basal means at the base or bottom
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Rock lies at the lowest stratum, starting from the surface down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning on top' sounds like a layering instruction, but it just supplies the first letter of 'top' to finish the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Basalt is a dark volcanic igneous stone, the commonest kind formed from cooled lava.

clue.text: Cryptically disguise noun “cunning” as an adjective

definitions.note: the clue itself adds that the answer is the adjective sense

indicators.note: something written cryptically is encoded and scrambled, so the letters need rearranging

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson asks how to disguise a noun so that it works as an adjective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noun' and 'adjective' look like grammar talk; 'noun' is fodder, and 'as an adjective' tells you 'cunning' is the descriptive sense, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A disingenuous person is insincere and pretends to know less than they do, a crafty, sly quality.

clue.text: Chance a noted clinic for reconstructive work

indicators.note: reconstructive work rebuilds something into a new shape, so the letters are reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hopes for a slot at a famous plastic surgery clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chance' reads as a noun meaning opportunity; here it is the adjective, as in a chance meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A chance encounter happens by accident without planning, which is what a coincidental one is.

clue.text: Tentatively be one hundred per cent like Thomas?

blocks.note: doubting Thomas, the apostle who would not believe without proof
a hundred per cent means completely

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly tries to be wholly like the sceptical apostle.
explanation.walkthrough: To be like Thomas is to doubt; doing so a hundred per cent is to doubt fully, which reads as the adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting tentatively means hesitating and lacking confidence, much as someone uncertain behaves.

clue.text: Knocking down protest hero full of appeal

indicators.note: to be full of something is to have it inside, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: a demo is a demonstration or protest march
a lion is a celebrated, brave person
it is slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A protest leader full of charisma is getting knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex appeal is an old convention, from the 1920s 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Demolition is the act of pulling down or destroying a building, the noun for flattening structures.

clue.text: Long time after old Papa Haydn’s works?

indicators.note: coming after something means following it, so this piece is placed second in the chain

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
Papa is the radio alphabet word for P
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Long after his death, 'Papa' Haydn, the composer's nickname, is still known for his music.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious reading is operas as staged music, but here it is the Latin plural of opus, the numbered works of a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus is the Latin word for a musical composition, and its plural form names a set of compositions.

clue.text: Having some power to bond with opponent in camp

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a rival is a competitor or opponent
campers sleep in a tent

explanation.surface: Someone at a camp tries to get on with an opponent sharing the site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power to bond' sounds social, but it is chemistry: valency is the bonding capacity of an atom.
explanation.definitionFit: A trivalent atom has a valency of three, so it can form three chemical links with other atoms.

clue.text: Peace agreement with power bombing cities

indicators.note: bombing blows things apart, so these letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: the arm of the law is its power, its reach
taken as written

explanation.surface: A peace treaty is signed while one power is still bombing cities.
explanation.walkthrough: The bombing is the anagram signal; ARM in the sense of power or authority, as in 'the long arm of the law'.
explanation.definitionFit: An armistice is a formal truce in which warring parties agree to stop fighting.

clue.text: What’s sticky and hard to throw away?

definitions.text: What’s sticky and hard to throw away?

blocks.note: surface reading: something gluey or adhesive
setter's reading: a wooden throwing stick that comes back after it is thrown

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticky' suggests glue that will not come off your hand; it means stick-like, a carved throwing stick that returns to the thrower.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian throwing weapon is a curved stick that flies back, so it cannot really be got rid of.

clue.text: Botch at least three notes

blocks.note: more than one mi, the third sol-fa note: at least two of them
do, the first sol-fa note, brings the count to at least three

explanation.surface: Someone fluffs a tune, bungling at least three of its notes.
explanation.walkthrough: MIS is the plural of the note mi, at least two of them, and DO is a third note, so the whole is at least three notes.
explanation.definitionFit: To misdo something is to perform it badly or wrongly, which is what botching a job means.

clue.text: Warmth of home shut up during day without end

indicators.note: something shut up during another is locked inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: Fri is the abbreviation for Friday
without end means having no end
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A cosy home is shut up all day, apparently endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without end' looks like a deletion signal, but it is a whole word, the adjective meaning everlasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmth in a person's manner is affection and kindness towards others, the quality of being amiable.

clue.text: French resort entertaining English relative

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to take them in, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A Riviera resort town plays host to a visiting English relation.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice the town has the same spelling as the adjective, which hides it nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is the daughter of one's brother or sister, a family member.

clue.text: Fixation over air in Lisbon

blocks.note: a fad is a short-lived craze or obsession
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A traveller describes an obsession with the atmosphere of Lisbon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' suggests atmosphere; it means a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Fado is the mournful traditional song of Portugal, performed in the bars of its capital.

clue.text: Crazy drinking energy drink

indicators.note: to drink something is to take it inside, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: mad means crazy
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone is wild about knocking back an energy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy drink' reads as one product, but 'drink' is split off as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mead is an old alcoholic beverage made by fermenting honey with water.

clue.text: Volume of Whitman contains nothing to kill time

indicators.note: to contain is to hold within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: Walt Whitman was American, and liter is the American spelling of litre, a unit of volume
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A book of Whitman's poems contains nothing but ways to pass the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' suggests a book of poems, but it is the measure, spelt the American way because Whitman was American.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to hang about idly with no purpose, wasting hours, which is what killing time means.

clue.text: Carelessly mention a name

indicators.note: something done carelessly is messed up, so the letters end up in a jumbled order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lets a name slip without thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name' looks like the object of 'mention'; it is the verb, to put forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To name someone for a post or award is to propose them as a candidate formally.

clue.text: Yankee has to consider carefully when there’s no parking over there

indicators.note: having no parking means a car-park sign letter is absent, so it is taken away

blocks.note: Yankee is the radio alphabet word for Y
to ponder is to think something over

explanation.surface: An American has to think hard where there is nowhere to leave the car.
explanation.walkthrough: P for parking is the road-sign letter, so PONDER loses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonder is an old or dialect word pointing at something at a distance, away in that direction.

clue.text: Eros perhaps appearing centrally in last item from Aida

indicators.note: centrally means at the core, so only the middle letters of each word are kept

blocks.note: the two central letters
the two central letters
the two central letters
the two central letters

explanation.surface: The god of love turns up at the heart of the final number in Verdi's opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last item from Aida' sounds like the opera's finale, but each of the four words gives up its two middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is a near-Earth minor planet, the first of its kind discovered, so it is an example of a space rock.
